1
.This Memo provides guidance on the Universal Credit Act 2025 and The Universal Credit and 
Employment and Support Allowance (Rates of Allowances
) (Amendment) 
Regulations 2026, in so far as 
they relate the Limited Capability for Work and Work-related Activity (LWCRA) Element of Universal 
Credit. The relevant sections of the Act and regulations come into force on 
06/04/26
 
and the relevant 
regulations have effect only in relation to assessment periods commencing on or after 
06/04/26
.
1

2.
 
The main change is that there will now be two rates for the LCWRA Element – a lower rate for those 
who are newly determined to have LCWRA 
on or after
 06/04/26 and a higher rate for those who were 
already determined to have LCWRA 
prior to 06/
04/26 (or who meet other criteria set out in paragraph 4).

3. 
If a claimant has a determination of LCWRA made 
on or
 
after
 
06/04/26, and they do not fall into any 
of the groups listed in paragraph 4 below, they will receive the lower rate of the LCWRA Element. From 
06/04/26 to 05/4/27 that lower rate is 
£217.2
6
 per assessment period
1
.

4.
 
 
The LCWRA Element will be paid at a higher rate for those claimants who are:

5.
 
From 06/04/26 to 05/04/27 that higher rate is 
£429.80
 per assessment period.
2

6
. A pre-2026 claimant is someone who:

6.1
. was entitled to the LCWRA Element before 06/04/26, 
and

6.2.
 
has been entitled to an award of UC which included the LCWRA Element continuously.
1

7.
 
When deciding whether the UC award with the LCWRA Element is ‘continuous’ no account is to be 
taken of a period of non-entitlement due to not meeting the financial condition of entitlement (i.e. the 
award would be less than a penny), as long as that period of non-entitlement has a duration of fewer 
than six months
1
.

8. 
A claimant will also be classed as a pre-2026 claimant, where:

8.1
 
a claimant’s pending assessment is yet to be undertaken on 05/04/26, and a determination of 
LCWRA is made on or after 06/04/26, 
or

8.2
 
a claimant has LCW and is awaiting a further assessment on 05/04/26, and a determination 
of LCWRA is made on or after 06/04/26, 
or

8.3
. a claimant has been determined LCWRA but on 06/04/26 the relevant period is yet to be 
served, 
or

8.4
. a claimant had an award of Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) which included the 
Support Component prior to 06/04/26 and continued to be entitled to ESA with the Support 
Component after 06/04/26 and 
up to the date on which a UC award which includes an LCWRA 
Element is made, 
and

the claimant has been continuously entitled to the LCWRA element since
1
.

9.
 
A terminally ill person is someone suffering from a progressive disease where death in consequence 
of that disease can reasonably be expected within 12 months.
1
 A terminally ill person is treated as 
having LCWRA.
2

10.
 
An SCC claimant is someone who:

10.1
. has been determined to have LCWRA on the basis of an assessment using the LCWRA 
activity schedule
1
, 
and

10.2
. at least one of the descriptors in the LWCRA activity schedule will apply to the claimant 
constantly and for the rest of their life
2
, 
and

10
.
3 
the specific bodily disease or disablement, or specific mental illness or disablement, which 
gave rise to the satisfaction of the descriptor, must be one the claimant will have for the rest of 
their life
3
, 
and

10
.
4 
the specific bodily disease or disablement, or specific mental illness or disablement, must 
have been diagnosed by an appropriately qualified health care professional in the course of the 
provision of NHS services
4
.

Note:
 ‘
NHS Services’ means health care services provided under s1(1) of the National Health Service 
Act 2006, s1(1) of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, s1(1) of the National Health Service 
(Scotland) Act 
1978, 
and health and social care provided within the Health and Social Care (Reform) Act 
(Northern Ireland) 2009, provided for the purpose set out at s2(1) of that Act.
1

11. 
In 
10.2
. ‘constantly’ means the descriptor applies to the claimant at all times or, as the case may be, 
on all occasions on which the claimant undertakes or attempts to undertake the activity described that 
descriptor
1
.

12
. Once a claimant has been determined as being an SCC claimant, or as not being an SCC claimant, 
no further assessment for this purpose is to be carried out unless evidence suggests that

12.1
. the determination was made in ignorance of, or based on a mistake as to, some material 
fact, 
or

12.2.
 
there has been a relevant change of circumstances in relation to the claimant’s physical or 
mental condition.
1

13.
 Where a claimant fails to provide information requested for an SCC assessment (without good 
reason) the claimant may be treated as not being an SCC claimant (providing the claimant was sent a 
further request to provide the information at least 3 weeks after the date of first request and at least 1 
week has passed since the further request was sent).
1

14. 
A claimant can be called to attend a medical examination for the purposes of an SCC assessment 
and a failure to attend or submit to that examination (without good reason) will result in them being 
treated as not being an SCC claimant (providing notice of the date, time and place of the examination 
was given 7 days in advance, or if the notice was for fewer than 7 days the claimant had agreed to 
that).
1
